Squalor

SKWAH-ler -- from Latin squalere ('to be rough, dirty, neglected'); related to the adjective squalid. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Squalor is a state of extreme dirtiness and neglect, especially resulting from poverty.

Aid workers documented the squalor of the flooded refugee camp: overflowing gutters, collapsing tents, and no clean water for miles.

Worked Example

After the factory closed, whole blocks of the neighborhood slid into squalor within a few short years.

Without jobs or income, the buildings and streets fell into a state of extreme neglect and dirt -- that decline is exactly what squalor names.

How Squalor Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

filth

filth: disgusting dirt or refuse

destitution

destitution: the state of being extremely poor and lacking basic necessities

Antonyms

opulence

opulence: great wealth and luxury

cleanliness

cleanliness: the state of being clean and well-kept

How Strong Is It? — filth → squalor → destitution

filth vs. squalor

filth vs. squalor: Filth is milder than squalor: an alley behind a restaurant can fill with filth in a few weeks, but squalor is graver — dirt and neglect so extreme that people are living inside it.

destitution vs. squalor

destitution vs. squalor: Destitution goes further than squalor: squalor is living amid extreme dirt and neglect, while war-ruined villages sink into destitution — a graver state with no food, shelter, or clean water left at all.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of squalor.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — squal-

root — squal-: rough, dirty, neglected (Latin (squalere))

suffix — -or

suffix — -or: state or condition of; forms a noun (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Latin squalere meant 'to be rough or dirty,' and the suffix -or names a state or condition. Squalor is the state of complete neglect -- everything left filthy and uncared for.

Use the root in a new word: squalid

Use the root in a new word: squalid: Squalid, the adjective form, describes a place or condition marked by squalor -- 'the squalid tenement building.'

Squalor specifically points to poverty-driven filth and neglect -- a broken, dirty living condition -- rather than simple messiness or a single dirty object.
